title: NestJS Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Make a controller route
entries.summary: A controller holds request handlers. @Get maps GET /hello to its method.
notes: A controller must be listed in a module to be used.

entries.name: Return named data
entries.summary: Nest sends returned objects as JSON. Open GET /book.
notes: Let Nest write the returned object instead of writing a second response.

entries.name: Read a route parameter
entries.summary: @Param reads a named part of the route. Open GET /hello/Ravi.
notes: A TypeScript type does not validate a value sent over HTTP.

entries.name: Read a query value
entries.summary: @Query reads the query string. Visit GET /search?q=cat.
notes: Validate query input before using it for important work.

entries.name: Check and parse a number
entries.summary: ParseIntPipe reads an integer or rejects bad input. GET /double/4 uses the checked number.
notes: The pipe does the runtime check; the number annotation alone does not.

entries.name: Read a request body
entries.summary: @Body supplies parsed JSON. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}.
notes: Check body fields instead of trusting the TypeScript shape.

entries.name: Share a service
entries.summary: A provider is a shared helper supplied by Nest. The controller asks for Books in its constructor. Open GET /book.
notes: List Books in module providers so Nest can create it.

entries.name: Supply a default query
entries.summary: DefaultValuePipe supplies a value before ParseIntPipe checks it. Open GET /page with no query.
notes: Pipe order matters: the default should happen before parsing.

entries.name: Choose a reply status
entries.summary: @HttpCode changes a handler status. POST /check returns 200 instead of the usual Nest POST status.
notes: A status describes the reply; it does not change the returned data.

entries.name: Add a response header
entries.summary: @Header adds metadata to a response. Open GET /note and inspect its Cache-Control header.
notes: Headers must be set before a response is sent.

entries.name: Send a client to another route
entries.summary: @Redirect sends a location to the client. A browser following GET /start ends at /hello.
notes: A redirect makes the client send a new request.

entries.name: Report a missing item
entries.summary: A built-in exception creates an HTTP error response. GET /missing reports a missing book.
notes: Use a suitable HTTP error instead of returning a success status for a failure.
